meta.title: Hotel mini shampoo bottles sold per year (world)

prompt: How many hotel-sized mini bottles of shampoo are sold worldwide every year?

clarifications.answer: Use a supply-side approach: hotels stocking bottles, occupancy, and per-room usage.
Assume about 4000 major cities worldwide, ~15 hotels each of which ~10 provide shampoo bottles, ~50 rooms per hotel.
Assume 100% occupancy for 25% of the year and 50% for the rest, i.e. about 62.5% average occupancy.
Rooms split 30% studio / 40% suite (1 bottle per 2-day stay) and 30% family (2 bottles per 2-day stay).

common_traps: Assuming full occupancy year-round instead of blending peak and off-peak into an average.
Charging one bottle per room-night instead of accounting for multi-day stays (half a bottle per day).
Forgetting that only a fraction of hotels provide shampoo bottles at all.

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no hotels-times-occupancy-times-usage chain.
anchors.3: Builds a supply chain but omits occupancy or the per-day usage conversion.
anchors.5: Derives occupied rooms per day and converts multi-day usage into bottles per day, then per year.

anchors.1: One flat usage rate for all rooms.
anchors.3: Splits rooms but with usage not tied to stay length.
anchors.5: Splits rooms by type with distinct bottles-per-stay, converted to a per-day rate.

anchors.1: Loses track of the daily-to-yearly scaling; lands orders of magnitude off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 20-40 crore.
anchors.5: Carries the occupancy and per-day math cleanly, landing near 30 crore bottles.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks against ~1.25 million occupied rooms daily worldwide, which is a plausible major-city hotel base.
